subject: Request: Headroom waiver & queued-throughput carveout for Dedicated Pool - Aurora Networks
messages:
From: Jane DuBois <jane.dubois@aurora-networks.com>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@aurora-networks.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated pool headroom / queued throughput request

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We finished a short QOS analysis of our inference workload and have a situational ask: our models drive timed batches every 30s that briefly spike concurrent sequence lengths and token rates. During campaign windows (monthly billing runs) the traffic pattern reliably creates a short-lived 5–7 minute burst where queueing behavior matters a lot.

Our current contract references a 99.9% throughput SLA across the dedicated pool but we need a carveout/waiver for these scheduled campaign windows to avoid repeated breach flags — Aurora is seeking a temporary headroom exception so auto-scaling doesn't count those scheduled bursts against the baseline SLA. We attached a short analysis (aurora-qos-analysis.pdf) and included a rough schedule for the next three months.

Can Redwood propose operational guardrails (e.g., scheduled prewarm, temporary burst lanes, crediting rules) or contract language we can share with procurement? Procurement will insist on clear MTRs/credits for any carveout.

Appreciate your help — we want to avoid paying for large overprovisioning but also avoid SLA noise.

Best,
Jane DuBois
Head of ML Ops | Aurora Networks
attachments: aurora-qos-analysis.pdf

From: alex.martinez@redwood.ai
To: jane.dubois@aurora-networks.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800

Jane — thanks for the clear writeup and attachment.

Quick note to confirm we received the analysis and will put together two things: (1) an operational mitigation proposal (prewarm + reserved burst lanes + canary plan) and (2) a suggested contract amendment that defines scheduled campaign windows, measurable signals, and crediting rules.

Ben — copying you to validate the technical feasibility and latency/queueing impacts on the current dedicated pool configuration for Aurora's pool id (AN-dedicated-03). Grace — can you flag procurement touchpoints and the typical credit formulas we use for scheduled maintenance-like carveouts?

I'll send an internal assessment this afternoon with a proposed customer-facing amendment.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: alex.martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, jane.dubois@aurora-networks.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool headroom / queued throughput request

On Mon, Nov 9, 2026 at 10:03 AM alex.martinez@redwood.ai wrote:
> Ben — copying you to validate the technical feasibility and latency/queueing impacts on the current dedicated pool configuration for Aurora's pool id (AN-dedicated-03).

Short assessment below (high level). Happy to hop on a quick call with Aurora if helpful.

Findings:
- Workload shape: brief, high-concurrency bursts (~3–7 min) with elevated avg seq length. Baseline throughput target is 18k tokens/sec for the pool; bursts push instantaneous token rates to ~22–24k tokens/sec.
- Current queueing policy: FIFO with soft-priority for pinned jobs; during bursts we observe increased p99 latency (x3) and increased app-layer retries.

Operational options (tradeoffs):
1) Scheduled prewarm + transient capacity: allocate 10–15% extra nodes for scheduled windows; keeps p99 latency within SLA but increases committed cost; requires contract allowance for scheduled reserved headroom.
2) Temporary burst lanes: create a 'burst' routing class with lower SLO (higher p99 threshold) and explicit waiver window; traffic routed there won't count against baseline throughput SLA. Requires policy + customer signoff and smaller crediting when traffic hits burst lanes.
3) Canary + throttled ramp: run canary on 10% of traffic for the first campaign, gather metrics, then expand. Minimizes risk and gives empirical breach probability.
4) Token-level prefork caching and KV warmup: reduces cold-start amplification during bursts; engineering lift moderate.

Proposed combination (recommended): implement (2) burst lanes + (3) canary + (4) KV warmup as immediate steps. For the contract side, propose a limited waiver: up to 4 scheduled windows/month, each window up to 10 minutes where traffic routed to burst lanes will not be counted as SLA violations provided Aurora notifies Redwood 48 hours in advance and provides the campaign schedule. If an unannounced spike occurs, normal SLA rules apply.

Metrics we'd require for the amendment: exact campaign windows, max expected concurrent requests, and a baseline token/sec target for the dedicated pool. Also propose a small 'scheduled-exception' credit of 5% of monthly committed spend for any missed availability during an agreed window (instead of the standard larger credit formula).

I'll draft a technical appendix with exact routing policy fields and retention of tracing for post-mortem.

—Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Jane DuBois <jane.dubois@aurora-networks.com>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, ops@aurora-networks.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool headroom / queued throughput request

Alex / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and concrete options. The proposed "burst lanes + canary" approach sounds workable. A few procurement/legal questions before we proceed to amendment:

1) Ramp schedule: we'll want a gradual ramp (one campaign run on canary in November, full roll in December) — acceptable?
2) Credits: procurement is pushing back on a flat 5% credit. They want a more graduated credit table if the burst lane itself fails to meet a minimum p50/p99 threshold (they proposed something like 2% for minor deviations, 10% for major).
3) Auditability: we need preserved traces and an event log for any time traffic was routed to burst lanes. Can Redwood provide a signed daily CSV export for the month after each scheduled window for audit?

If Redwood can accept the ramp (1) and provide the audit export (3), we'll be OK to negotiate the credit band (2). Also please confirm whether the burst lanes will be isolated to Aurora's dedicated pool (AN-dedicated-03) or shared with other tenants. Isolation is important to us.

Regards,
Jane

From: alex.martinez@redwood.ai
To: jane.dubois@aurora-networks.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool headroom / queued throughput request

Jane — thanks, and summary & next steps below.

Summary of agreed commercial/operational terms (pending legal/contract amendment):
- Technical guardrail: implement "burst" routing class for AN-dedicated-03, isolated to Aurora's pool (no cross-tenant sharing).
- Pilot schedule: canary during November campaign (single run), evaluate metrics, full roll December campaign if success.
- Notification: Aurora will provide campaign windows >=48 hours in advance.
- Audit/export: Redwood will provide a signed CSV export (routing events + per-request latency/p95/p99) for the month following each scheduled window.
- Credits: we will propose a graduated credit table in the amendment. Redwood's starting proposal: 2% minor deviation, 8% major deviation, final language to be negotiated.

Attached is a draft amendment and an internal tech appendix link for your review: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/sales/docs/aurora-amendment-v1. Grace, please coordinate procurement expectations and start a legal ticket to draft the formal amendment (link included).

Next steps:
- Redwood to share amendment + routing policy + tech appendix by EOD Nov 10 (Alex/Ben).
- Aurora procurement to confirm ramp acceptance and propose final credit bands by Nov 12.
- Schedule follow-up call if needed (I'll propose times).

Thanks all — we'll keep this scoped and limited to avoid SLA churn.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attachments: proposed-amendment-v1.docx
